info.title: Nutanix Lifecycle Management APIs
info.description: Manage Infrastructure, Software and Firmware Upgrades.

tags.name: FoundationCentralConfig
tags.description: Manage global settings and configurations for Foundation Central. Use these APIs to retrieve and update Foundation Central configuration settings such as timeout configurations that control the behavior of the Foundation Central.

tags.name: ClaimTokens
tags.description: Manage claim tokens used for secure node registration with Foundation Central. Claim tokens provide a secure mechanism for nodes to authenticate and register themselves with Foundation Central during the onboarding process. Use these APIs to create, retrieve, update, and delete claim tokens, as well as retrieve the associated secrets required for node authentication.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description: Manage the complete lifecycle of nodes in Foundation Central. Use these APIs to onboard new nodes, retrieve node details, update node configurations, and remove nodes from management. Additionally, perform node imaging operations to deploy operating systems and hypervisors, configure hardware provider settings on nodes, and refresh node information from external sources.

tags.name: HardwareProviders
tags.description: Manage integrations with external hardware providers such as bare-metal and data center management systems. Use these APIs to list available hardware providers, retrieve provider details, and manage connections to provider endpoints. Each hardware provider connection enables node discovery capabilities, allowing Foundation Central to automatically detect and onboard nodes from the connected infrastructure.

tags.name: InstallerImages
tags.description: Manage installer images used for node imaging operations in Foundation Central. Installer images contain the AOS, hypervisor or host OS software required to provision nodes. Use these APIs to register new installer images from external URLs, list available images, retrieve image details, and remove images that are no longer needed.

tags.name: PatchedImages
tags.description: Manage patched images that combine base installer images with additional patches and updates. Patched images provide a streamlined way to deploy nodes with pre-applied software updates, security patches, and custom configurations. Use these APIs to create patched images from base images, list available patched images, retrieve image details, and delete patched images.

tags.name: Config
tags.description: Manage the LCM framework configuration for a cluster. The configuration controls settings such as the LCM repository URL, auto-inventory scheduling, HTTPS enforcement, and connectivity mode (connected-site vs. dark-site). Use GET /config to retrieve the current configuration and PUT /config to update it. Changing the configuration returns an asynchronous task reference. The X-Cluster-Id header can be used to target a specific Prism Element cluster when operating from Prism Central. See the Config model for the full list of configurable and read-only properties.

tags.name: Entities
tags.description: Query the software and firmware entities discovered by LCM on a cluster. Entities represent individual upgradable components such as AOS, AHV, NCC, BMC firmware, BIOS, and disk firmware. Each entity includes its current version, available upgrade versions, location (node or cluster scope), and dependency information. Use GET /entities to list all entities with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /entities/{extId} to retrieve a single entity by its identifier. Use POST /entities/$actions/export to export the full entity inventory as a downloadable file. Entities are populated by the Inventory operation (POST /$actions/inventory); if no inventory has been run, the entities list will be empty. To preload upgrade images for entities before an upgrade, use POST /$actions/preload-artifacts.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Compute and retrieve upgrade notifications that describe the impact of a planned upgrade on cluster nodes and entities. Notifications inform the user about disruptive actions (such as host reboots, VM migrations, or maintenance-mode entry) that will occur during the upgrade. To generate notifications, first call POST /$actions/compute-notifications with the intended entity update specifications. This returns an asynchronous task; once the task completes, retrieve the resource identifier from the task completion_details and use GET /notifications/{extId} to fetch the computed notification results. Notifications include severity levels (INFO, WARNING, NOTICE) and are grouped by entity or location.

tags.name: Recommendations
tags.description: Compute and retrieve upgrade recommendations for a set of entities. Recommendations resolve dependencies, identify additional required updates, and produce a validated list of entity-update specifications ready for use in prechecks and upgrades. To generate recommendations, call POST /$actions/compute-recommendations with one of four input types: entity types (SOFTWARE/FIRMWARE), target entities, entity update specs, or deploy specs. This returns an asynchronous task; once the task completes, retrieve the resource identifier from the task completion_details and use GET /recommendations/{extId} to fetch the computed recommendation results. The result includes the resolved entityUpdateSpecs, any skipped, modifiable, or addable entities, and deployable versions.

tags.name: Upgrades
tags.description: Perform an upgrade operation to update one or more LCM entities to their target versions. Before invoking an upgrade, run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover entities, compute recommendations (POST /$actions/compute-recommendations) to resolve dependencies, and optionally run prechecks (POST /$actions/prechecks) to validate readiness. The upgrade endpoint (POST /$actions/upgrade) accepts an UpgradeSpec containing entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs), optional management server credentials for ESX/Hyper-V clusters, and auto-handle flags for VM management during maintenance mode. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference; monitor the task via the Prism tasks API. Use GET /status to check whether an upgrade is already in progress on the cluster.

tags.name: Prechecks
tags.description: Run pre-upgrade validation checks to verify that the cluster and its entities are ready for an upgrade. Prechecks detect conditions that would cause an upgrade to fail, such as insufficient disk space, incompatible configurations, or pinned VMs that cannot be migrated. Call POST /$actions/prechecks with a PrechecksSpec containing the same entityUpdateSpecs you intend to pass to the upgrade endpoint. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference; inspect the task result to determine whether all prechecks passed. If prechecks fail, address the reported issues before proceeding to upgrade (POST /$actions/upgrade). The skippedPrecheckFlags field can be used to bypass specific prechecks such as the pinned-VM check.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: Trigger an inventory operation to discover all upgradable software and firmware entities on a cluster. Inventory scans the cluster nodes, identifies installed components and their versions, and checks the configured LCM repository for available updates. Call POST /$actions/inventory to start the operation; an optional InventorySpec body allows you to specify the inventory type (FULL, SOFTWARE, NODE, or RESCAN) and provide vendor management credentials for third-party hardware. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference. Once inventory completes, the discovered entities are available via GET /entities and the cluster summary is updated in GET /lcm-summaries. Inventory must be run at least once before computing recommendations or performing upgrades.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Query the LCM images that have been downloaded to the cluster for use in upgrades. An image represents one or more binary files (ISO, tar, firmware payload) associated with a specific entity class, model, and version. Images are downloaded automatically during an upgrade or can be pre-staged using the preload-artifacts operation (POST /$actions/preload-artifacts). Use GET /images to list all downloaded images with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Each image includes file metadata (size, checksum, file path) and release notes.

tags.name: Status
tags.description: Retrieve the current operational status of the LCM framework on a cluster. The status includes the installed LCM framework version, whether a framework update is available, any in-progress operation (inventory, prechecks, upgrade, or upload) with its task identifier, the cancel-intent flag, URL accessibility, connectivity type, and restricted-mode information. Use GET /status before starting a new operation to confirm no conflicting operation is already running. The X-Cluster-Id header can be used to target a specific Prism Element cluster.

tags.name: LcmSummaries
tags.description: Retrieve high-level summaries of LCM state across one or more clusters in a Prism Central environment. Each summary includes the installed LCM version, available framework version, hardware vendor, connectivity type, cluster capabilities (such as MCL inventory/upgrade support), and indicators for URL accessibility and available upgrades. Use GET /lcm-summaries to list summaries for all registered clusters with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /lcm-summaries/{extId} to retrieve the summary for a specific cluster. Summaries are updated after each inventory or upgrade operation.

tags.name: UpgradeSelections
tags.description: Manage saved upgrade selections for dark-site upgrade workflows. An upgrade selection captures the set of entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs) that a user intends to upgrade on a specific cluster. Use POST /upgrade-selections to save a selection, GET /upgrade-selections to list saved selections, and GET /upgrade-selections/{extId} to retrieve a specific selection. Use POST /upgrade-selections/{extId}/$actions/export to generate a download_helper.zip file containing scripts and instructions for downloading the required dark-site bundles from the Nutanix Portal. Once bundles are uploaded to the cluster, the selection status transitions from PENDING_UPLOAD to UPGRADE_READY, and the user can proceed with prechecks and upgrade using the saved entityUpdateSpecs. Use DELETE /upgrade-selections/{extId} to remove a selection that is no longer needed.

tags.name: LcmHistories
tags.description: Query the history of LCM operations (inventory, upgrade, bundle upload) performed across all clusters in a Prism Central environment. Each history entry records the operation type, start and end times, overall status, the user who initiated the operation, the LCM framework version at the time of execution, and detailed component information (entities upgraded, versions, per-entity status). Use GET /lcm-histories to list history entries with support for pagination, filtering (by operation type, status, cluster, time range), sorting, and field projection. Use GET /lcm-histories/{extId} to retrieve a single history entry. Use POST /lcm-histories/$actions/export to export history data as a downloadable file.

tags.name: Bundles
tags.description: Manage LCM upgrade bundles on a cluster. A bundle is a packaged archive containing one or more upgrade images for software or firmware entities. Bundles are used primarily in dark-site environments where the cluster does not have direct internet connectivity. Use POST /bundles to upload a new bundle (specifying the vendor, type, and optional URL source or checksum). Use GET /bundles to list all bundles on the cluster with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /bundles/{extId} to retrieve details of a specific bundle. Use DELETE /bundles/{extId} to remove a bundle that is no longer needed. After uploading a bundle, run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover the newly available updates.

get.summary: Retrieve details of a specific LCM bundle.
get.description: Retrieve the full details of a specific LCM bundle by its external identifier. The response includes the bundle name, size, type (SOFTWARE, FIRMWARE, PRODUCT_META, FRAMEWORK, or IMAGE_BUNDLE), vendor, creation timestamp, contained images, checksum, and upload mode. Bundles are used primarily in dark-site deployments to deliver upgrade images to a cluster that lacks internet connectivity.

parameters.name: extId
parameters.description: The external identifier (UUID) of the LCM bundle.

200.description: The full Bundle object for the requested identifier. See the Bundle model for all available properties.

delete.summary: Delete an LCM bundle from the cluster.
delete.description: Delete an LCM bundle and its associated images from the cluster. This operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; poll the task to confirm deletion completed. Deleting a bundle removes the upgrade images it contains, which may affect the ability to perform upgrades for the corresponding entities until new images are provided. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency.

parameters.name: extId
parameters.description: The external identifier (UUID) of the LCM bundle.

parameters.name: NTNX-Request-Id
parameters.description: A unique identifier that is associated with each request. The provided value must be opaque and preferably in Universal Unique Identifier (UUID) format. This identifier is also used as an idempotence token for safely retrying requests in case of network errors. All the supported Nutanix API clients add this auto-generated request identifier to each request.

202.description: A TaskReference for the asynchronous bundle deletion operation.

get.summary: List all LCM bundles on the cluster.
get.description: Retrieve a paginated list of all LCM bundles present on the cluster. Supports standard query parameters for pagination ($page, $limit), filtering ($filter), sorting ($orderby), and field projection ($select). Each bundle entry includes metadata such as name, type, vendor, size, and creation time. For dark-site deployments, bundles are the primary mechanism for delivering upgrade images to the cluster.

parameters.name: $page
parameters.description: A URL query parameter that specifies the page number of the result set. It must be a positive integer between 0 and the maximum number of pages that are available for that resource. Any number out of this range might lead to no results. If both $page and $apply query parameters are present, $page will be applied on entities within the groups.

schema.description: A URL query parameter that specifies the page number of the result set. It must be a positive integer between 0 and the maximum number of pages that are available for that resource. Any number out of this range might lead to no results. If both $page and $apply query parameters are present, $page will be applied on entities within the groups.

parameters.name: $limit
parameters.description: A URL query parameter that specifies the total number of records returned in the result set.  Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Any number out of this range will lead to a validation error. If the limit is not provided, a default value of 50 records will be returned in the result set. If both $limit and $apply query parameters are present, $limit  will be applied on entities within the groups. Default value of limit with $apply will be 5.

schema.description: A URL query parameter that specifies the total number of records returned in the result set.  Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Any number out of this range will lead to a validation error. If the limit is not provided, a default value of 50 records will be returned in the result set. If both $limit and $apply query parameters are present, $limit  will be applied on entities within the groups. Default value of limit with $apply will be 5.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description:
A URL query parameter that allows clients to filter a collection of resources. The expression specified with $filter is evaluated for each resource in the collection, and only items where the expression evaluates to true are included in the response. Expression specified with the $filter must conform to the [OData V4.01](https://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/odata/v4.01/odata-v4.01-part1-protocol.html) URL conventions.
For example, filter **$filter=name eq 'karbon-ntnx-1.0'** would filter the result on cluster name 'karbon-ntnx1.0', filter **$filter=startswith(name, 'C')** would filter on cluster name starting with 'C'. If both $filter and $apply query parameters are present, $filter will be applied on entities within the groups.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description: A URL query parameter that allows clients to specify the sort criteria for the returned list of objects. Resources can be sorted in ascending order using asc or descending order using desc. If asc or desc are not specified, the resources will be sorted in ascending order by default. For example, '$orderby=templateName desc' would get all templates sorted by templateName in descending order. If both $orderby and $apply query parameters are present, $orderby will be applied on entities within the groups.

parameters.name: $select
parameters.description: A URL query parameter that allows clients to request a specific set of properties for each entity or complex type. Expression specified with the $select must conform to the [OData V4.01](https://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/odata/v4.01/odata-v4.01-part1-protocol.html) URL conventions. If a $select expression consists of a single select item that is an asterisk (i.e., *), then all properties on the matching resource will be returned. If both $select and $apply query parameters are present, $select will be applied on entities within the groups.

post.summary: Create a new LCM bundle on the cluster (finalize after streaming to objects-lite via S3 PUT).
post.description: Create a new LCM bundle on the cluster. Bundle creation is a 2-step process. Step 1: Stream the bundle bits from the user's local setup to the objects-lite service using the AWS S3 PUT API. Use base64-encoded username and password of a Prism Admin or Super Admin user as credentials. Alternatively, if the bundle is hosted somewhere accessible (e.g., external server or Nutanix Portal), provide a URL source to avoid Step 1; LCM will download the bundle from the URL. Step 2: Finalize the bundle by calling this CreateBundle v4 API with the object key from Step 1 in the name field (or omit name when using URL source). The request body must include the bundle vendor and may include a checksum (for verification). The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; poll the task to track progress. After a bundle is successfully created, run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover the newly available updates from the bundle's images. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency.

parameters.name: NTNX-Request-Id
parameters.description: A unique identifier that is associated with each request. The provided value must be opaque and preferably in Universal Unique Identifier (UUID) format. This identifier is also used as an idempotence token for safely retrying requests in case of network errors. All the supported Nutanix API clients add this auto-generated request identifier to each request.

202.description: A TaskReference for the asynchronous bundle upload operation. Poll the task to track upload progress.

post.summary: Perform an inventory operation to discover upgradable entities on a cluster.
post.description: Trigger an inventory operation to discover all upgradable software and firmware entities on a cluster. Inventory scans cluster nodes, identifies installed components and their current versions, and checks the configured LCM repository for available updates. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; poll the task to track progress. Once completed, discovered entities are available via GET /entities and the cluster summary is updated in GET /lcm-summaries. An optional InventorySpec body allows specifying the inventory type and vendor management credentials. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. Only one inventory operation can run on a cluster at a time; check GET /status before invoking. In dark-site mode, inventory discovers available updates only from bundles that have been uploaded to the cluster (POST /bundles); it does not contact the Nutanix portal.

parameters.name: NTNX-Request-Id
parameters.description: A unique identifier that is associated with each request. The provided value must be opaque and preferably in Universal Unique Identifier (UUID) format. This identifier is also used as an idempotence token for safely retrying requests in case of network errors. All the supported Nutanix API clients add this auto-generated request identifier to each request.

parameters.name: X-Cluster-Id
parameters.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

parameters.name: $dryrun
parameters.description: A URL query parameter that allows long running operations to execute in a dry-run mode providing ability to identify trouble spots and system failures without performing the actual operation. Additionally this mode also offers a summary snapshot of the resultant system in order to better understand how things fit together. The operation runs in dry-run mode only if the provided value is true.

post.summary: Compute upgrade notifications for a set of LCM entities.
post.description: Compute upgrade notifications for a set of LCM entities and their target versions. Notifications describe the impact of the planned upgrade on cluster nodes and entities, including disruptive actions such as host reboots, VM migrations, and maintenance-mode entry. Submit a NotificationsSpec containing entity update specifications (entity UUID and target version pairs) and optional credentials for third-party vendor management. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference. Once the task completes successfully, retrieve the resource identifier from the task's completion_details field and use GET /notifications/{extId} to fetch the computed notification results. The result resource is valid for 1 hour from creation. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency.

parameters.description: A unique identifier that is associated with each request. The provided value must be opaque and preferably in Universal Unique Identifier (UUID) format. post.summary: Run pre-upgrade validation checks for a planned upgrade.
post.description: Run pre-upgrade validation checks to verify that the cluster and its entities are ready for an upgrade. Prechecks detect conditions that would cause an upgrade to fail, such as insufficient disk space, cluster health issues, incompatible configurations, or pinned VMs that cannot be migrated during host maintenance mode. Submit a PrechecksSpec containing the entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs) that you intend to use for the upgrade. The entityUpdateSpecs should match the output from POST /$actions/compute-recommendations or be manually constructed from GET /entities data. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; inspect the task result to determine whether all prechecks passed. If prechecks fail, address the reported issues before proceeding to POST /$actions/upgrade. Use the skippedPrecheckFlags field to bypass specific prechecks (e.g. the pinned-VM check). Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency.

post.summary: Compute upgrade recommendations for a set of LCM entities.
post.description: Compute upgrade recommendations for a set of LCM entities. Recommendations resolve inter-entity dependencies, identify additional entities that must be co-upgraded, and produce a validated list of entityUpdateSpecs ready for use in prechecks (POST /$actions/prechecks) and upgrades (POST /$actions/upgrade). Submit a RecommendationSpec containing one of four input types: entity types (SOFTWARE/FIRMWARE) for broad recommendations, target entities for entity-class/model-based selection, entity update specs for specific UUID-to-version mappings, or deploy specs for pre-deployment planning. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference. Once the task completes successfully, retrieve the resource identifier from the task's completion_details field and use GET /recommendations/{extId} to fetch the computed recommendation results. The result resource is valid for 1 hour from creation. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency. In dark-site mode, recommendations are limited to updates available from uploaded bundles.

post.summary: Perform an upgrade operation on one or more LCM entities.
post.description: Perform an upgrade operation to update one or more LCM entities to their specified target versions. Before invoking an upgrade, ensure you have: (1) run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover entities, (2) computed recommendations (POST /$actions/compute-recommendations) to resolve dependencies and obtain validated entityUpdateSpecs, (3) optionally reviewed notifications (POST /$actions/compute-notifications) to understand the upgrade impact, and (4) run prechecks (POST /$actions/prechecks) to validate cluster readiness. Submit an UpgradeSpec containing the entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs). For ESX or Hyper-V clusters, provide the managementServer credentials. Use autoHandleFlags to allow LCM to automatically power off pinned VMs during maintenance mode and restore them after the upgrade. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; monitor the task via the Prism tasks API. Use GET /status to check whether an upgrade is already in progress. Only one upgrade can run on a cluster at a time. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency. In dark-site mode, ensure the required bundles have been uploaded (POST /bundles) before running the upgrade; images are not downloaded from the portal.

out the network details from developers and service deployers (dev-ops).
The name should be something that defines the positioning of the load balancer
in the data center. e.g. "corp", "wan", "dc", "it", "it-hr". Currently in a given
subdomain - the interface should be unique - which greatly simplifies what
the service deployer has to specify to expose the service.
A single load balancer defines one or more interfaces at load balancer creation time.

recommendationSpec.description: Specification for computing upgrade recommendations. Accepts one of four input types: an array of entity types (SOFTWARE/FIRMWARE) for broad recommendations, an array of target entities identified by class/model/version, an array of entity update specs with specific UUID-to-version mappings, or an array of deploy specs for pre-deployment planning.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.RecommendationS.description: Specification for computing upgrade recommendations. Accepts one of four input types: an array of entity types (SOFTWARE/FIRMWARE) for broad recommendations, an array of target entities identified by class/model/version, an array of entity update specs with specific UUID-to-version mappings, or an array of deploy specs for pre-deployment planning.

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.ComputeRecomme.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/operations/$actions/compute-recommendations Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityType.title: Entity type
lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityType.description: Classifies whether the entity is a software component or a firmware component.

x-enumDescriptions.FIRMWARE: Firmware entity type. Includes components such as BMC, BIOS, disk controller, and NIC firmware.
x-enumDescriptions.SOFTWARE: Software entity type. Includes components such as AOS, NCC, AHV, and LCM framework.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.TargetEntity.title: Target entity
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.TargetEntity.description: Identifies a specific entity for recommendation computation using its class, model, and desired target version. Optionally includes location information and device identifier for disambiguation when multiple instances of the same entity exist.

version.description: The target version that this entity has been selected to upgrade to. This field is set when an upgrade selection or upgrade operation has designated a specific version for this entity. Unset if no upgrade target has been chosen.

deviceId.description: A unique device identifier for the entity, such as a hard drive serial number, NIC serial number, or other hardware-specific identifier.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityDeploySpec.title: Entity deploy specification
lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityDeploySpec.description: Specifies an entity to deploy (pre-stage) on the cluster, identified by its base model properties (class, model, type, version, hardware family).

lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityBaseModel.title: Entity base model
lifecycle.v4.3.common.EntityBaseModel.description: Base model for LCM entities, containing the common properties shared across all entity types: entity class, model, type, current version, and hardware family. This model is extended by the full Entity model and is used as a building block in recommendations, notifications, history, and other contexts.

entityClass.description: The class or category of the entity (e.g. "Core Cluster", "Foundation", "Firmware"). The class groups related entity models together.

entityModel.description: The model or product name of the entity (e.g. "AOS", "NCC", "BMC", "AHV"). Uniquely identifies the specific component within its entity class.

entityVersion.description: The currently installed version of the entity on the cluster or node.

hardwareFamily.description: The hardware family designation for an entity (e.g. "dell_gen_12"), identifying the hardware generation and vendor platform the entity is compatible with.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LocationInfo.title: Entity location information

uuid.description: The UUID of the location (node, cluster, or Prism Central) where the resource resides.

locationName.description: The display name of the location (e.g. the hostname of a node).

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LocationInfo.description: Describes the location of an entity as a tuple of location type (NODE, CLUSTER, or PC) and the corresponding UUID.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LocationType.title: Location type
lifecycle.v4.3.common.LocationType.description: The scope level of an entity in the LCM hierarchy, indicating whether the entity belongs to a node, a cluster, or Prism Central.

x-enumDescriptions.PC: Prism Central-scoped entity. The entity applies at the Prism Central level.
x-enumDescriptions.NODE: Node-scoped entity. The entity belongs to a specific node within the cluster.
x-enumDescriptions.CLUSTER: Cluster-scoped entity. The entity applies to the entire cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.DeploySpec.title: Deploy specification

entityDeploySpecs.description: List of entity deploy specifications identifying which entities' images should be deployed to the cluster.

copyToObjectsLite.description: When true, deployed images are also copied to Objects Lite storage. The default value is false.

downloadSubEntityImagesOnly.description: When true, only sub-entity images are downloaded to the catalog, skipping the parent entity image. The default value is false.

downloadBaseImagesOnly.description: When true, only the base (parent) entity images are downloaded, skipping sub-entity images. The default value is false.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.DeploySpec.description: Specification for deploying (pre-staging) upgrade artifacts on a cluster. Contains a list of entity deploy specifications and optional flags for controlling image deployment behavior (e.g. copying to Objects Lite, downloading only sub-entity images).

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.InventorySpec.title: Inventory specification

credentials.description: Credentials to be provided by the user for LCM operations that require authentication with external systems such as vCenter or Intersight.

inventoryType.description: The scope of the inventory scan to perform.

nodeList.description: List of node UUIDs to inventory. Required when inventoryType is set to NODE; ignored for other inventory types.

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.InventorySpec.description: Optional specification for the inventory operation. When omitted, a full inventory is performed. Use inventoryType to select a specific scan scope (FULL, SOFTWARE, NODE, or RESCAN). Supply credentials for clusters with third-party vendor management (ESX vCenter, Cisco Intersight/UCS) so that LCM can discover firmware entities managed by those platforms. For NODE inventory type, also provide the nodeList with the UUIDs of nodes to scan.

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.InventoryApiRe.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/operations/$actions/inventory Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.InventoryType.title: Inventory type
lifecycle.v4.3.operations.InventoryType.description: The scope of the inventory scan to perform.

x-enumDescriptions.RESCAN: Rescan inventory. Re-checks the LCM repository for available updates without performing a full hardware scan of cluster nodes. Faster than a full inventory.
x-enumDescriptions.NODE: Node-scoped inventory. Scans only the specific nodes listed in the nodeList field of the InventorySpec. Requires nodeList to be provided.
x-enumDescriptions.FULL: Full inventory. Scans all nodes in the cluster for both software and firmware entities and checks the LCM repository for available updates.
x-enumDescriptions.SOFTWARE: Software-only inventory. Scans only software entities (e.g. AOS, NCC, LCM framework) without scanning firmware components.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.PrechecksSpec.title: Prechecks specification

entityUpdateSpecs.description: List of entity update specifications (entity UUID and target version pairs) for which to compute recommendations.

skippedPrecheckFlags.description: List of precheck flags to skip during the prechecks operation. The allowed value is 'POWER_OFF_UVMS' which skips the pinned-VM precheck that verifies all VMs can be migrated off a host before it enters maintenance mode.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.PrechecksSpec.description: Specification for running a prechecks operation. Contains the list of entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs) describing the intended upgrade, optional management server credentials for ESX/Hyper-V clusters, optional flags to skip specific prechecks (e.g. pinned-VM check), and optional vendor management credentials for third-party hardware.

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.PrechecksApiRe.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/operations/$actions/prechecks Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.common.ManagementServer.title: Management server configuration

ip.description: The IP address of the management server (vCenter for ESX, SCVMM for Hyper-V).

username.description: The username for authenticating with the management server.

password.description: The password for authenticating with the management server.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.ManagementServer.description: Configuration for the cluster management server, required when performing upgrades on clusters running ESX or Hyper-V hypervisors. Provides the credentials LCM needs to interact with vCenter or SCVMM during the upgrade process.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.SystemAutoMgmtFlag.description: A flag that controls automatic system operations during an upgrade, such as powering off or migrating VMs that would otherwise block host maintenance mode.

x-enumDescriptions.POWER_OFF_UVMS: Allow LCM to automatically power off user VMs that cannot be live-migrated during host maintenance mode. VMs are powered back on after the upgrade completes.
x-enumDescriptions.MIGRATE_POWERED_OFF_UVMS: Allow LCM to migrate powered-off user VMs to other hosts in the cluster while entering maintenance mode during the upgrade.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.HypervisorType.description: The type of hypervisor running on the cluster nodes.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.PreloadSpec.title: Preload specification

entityUpdateSpecs.description: List of entity update specifications (entity UUID and target version pairs) for which to compute recommendations.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.PreloadSpec.description: Specification for preloading upgrade artifacts. Contains a list of entity update specifications identifying which entities' images to download to the cluster ahead of an upgrade.

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.PreloadArtifac.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/operations/$actions/preload-artifacts Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.common.UpgradeSpec.title: Upgrade specification
lifecycle.v4.3.common.UpgradeSpec.description: Specification for performing an upgrade operation. Extends PrechecksSpec with additional fields for automatic VM management during host maintenance mode. Contains the entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs), optional management server credentials for ESX/Hyper-V clusters, optional autoHandleFlags for automatic VM power management, and maxWaitTimeInSecs for post-upgrade VM startup.

autoHandleFlags.description: List of automated system operations that LCM should perform during the upgrade to avoid precheck failures and restore state after the update completes. Allowed flags: - POWER_OFF_UVMS: Allows LCM to automatically power off user VMs that cannot be live-migrated to other hosts when a node enters maintenance mode, and power them back on when the update is done. - MIGRATE_POWERED_OFF_UVMS: Allows LCM to migrate powered-off VMs to other hosts in the cluster while entering maintenance mode during the upgrade.

maxWaitTimeInSecs.description: Maximum number of seconds LCM waits for VMs to come up after a host exits maintenance mode following an upgrade. Must be between 60 and 86400 seconds (1 minute to 24 hours).

lifecycle.v4.3.operations.UpgradeApiResp.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/operations/$actions/upgrade Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Bundle.title: LCM Bundle
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Bundle.description: Represents an LCM upgrade bundle containing one or more upgrade images. Bundles package software and firmware update payloads for delivery to clusters, primarily used in dark-site environments. Each bundle has a vendor (NUTANIX or THIRD_PARTY), a type, and may contain multiple images for different entities.

name.description: The display name of the bundle (e.g. "lcm_nos_6.10.tar.gz"). When creating a bundle via the 2-step upload flow, this must be the object key used in the S3 PUT request to the objects-lite service in Step 1.

sizeBytes.description: The total size of the bundle in bytes.

type.description: The type of the LCM bundle, indicating what kind of content it contains.

vendor.description: The vendor or owner that produced the bundle.

images.description: List of LCM images contained within this bundle. Each image represents an upgrade payload for a specific entity class and model.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

urlSource.description: Specifies a URL from which LCM should download the bundle content. Use this as an alternative to Step 1 (streaming via S3 PUT) when the bundle is hosted somewhere accessible, such as an external server or the Nutanix Portal.

uploadMode.description: The upload mode used for the bundle, indicating whether it was targeted to a specific cluster or uploaded centrally.

unqualifiedEntitiesDetail.description: List of entities within the bundle that were not applicable to the cluster during upload. Each entry explains which entity was unqualified and why.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleType.title: Bundle type
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleType.description: The type of the LCM bundle, indicating what kind of content it contains.

x-enumDescriptions.PRODUCT_META: A Product Meta compatibility bundle containing metadata that LCM uses to determine which updates are compatible with the current cluster configuration.
x-enumDescriptions.IMAGE_BUNDLE: A Nutanix image bundle for centralized uploads. Use this type when uploading Nutanix image bundles that should be distributed across multiple clusters.
x-enumDescriptions.FIRMWARE: Firmware entity type. Includes components such as BMC, BIOS, disk controller, and NIC firmware.
x-enumDescriptions.FRAMEWORK: An LCM framework bundle containing an update to the LCM framework itself.
x-enumDescriptions.SOFTWARE: Software entity type. Includes components such as AOS, NCC, AHV, and LCM framework.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleVendor.title: Bundle vendor
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleVendor.description: The vendor or owner that produced the bundle.

x-enumDescriptions.THIRD_PARTY: A third-party bundle containing updates from a hardware or software vendor other than Nutanix.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Image.title: LCM Image
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Image.description: An LCM image consisting of one or more binary files associated with a specific entity class, model, and version. Includes metadata such as release notes, file checksums, and qualification status.

releaseNotes.description: Release notes for this image, describing the changes, fixes, and improvements included in the update.

specVersion.description: The version of the image metadata specification used to describe this image.

isQualified.description: Indicates whether this third-party image version has been qualified (validated) for use with the current cluster configuration.

status.description: Classification of an available version indicating its release status and priority.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LcmSha256Sum.description: A SHA-256 checksum value used to verify the integrity of a bundle or image file.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LcmMd5Sum.title: MD5 checksum

lifecycle.v4.3.common.LcmMd5Sum.description: An MD5 checksum value used to verify the integrity of a bundle or image file.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleUploadMod.title: Bundle upload mode
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.BundleUploadMod.description: Indicates how the bundle was uploaded to the cluster.

x-enumDescriptions.TARGETED: Targeted upload mode. The bundle was uploaded specifically to a single cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.AvailableVersionSt.title: Available version status
lifecycle.v4.3.common.AvailableVersionSt.description: Classification of an available version indicating its release status and priority.

x-enumDescriptions.AVAILABLE: Available version. A general-availability release that can be applied.
x-enumDescriptions.EMERGENCY: Emergency version. An urgent release addressing a critical issue that requires immediate action.
x-enumDescriptions.RECOMMENDED: Recommended version. The vendor-recommended update for production use.
x-enumDescriptions.STS: Short-term supported (STS) version. Receives updates for a limited support window.
x-enumDescriptions.LTS: Long-term supported (LTS) version. Receives extended maintenance and security updates.
x-enumDescriptions.LATEST: Latest version. The most recent release available.
x-enumDescriptions.DEPRECATED: Deprecated version. No longer supported and should be replaced with a newer version.
x-enumDescriptions.ESTS: Extended short-term supported (ESTS) version. Receives updates for an extended support window beyond standard STS.

version.description: The version string of this component version (e.g. "20230302.211").

upgradeTargets.description: List of version strings that this component version can be upgraded to. Each entry represents a valid upgrade target.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Config.title: LCM Configuration
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Config.description: Represents the full configuration of the LCM framework on a cluster, including the repository URL, auto-inventory settings, framework version information, connectivity mode, and feature flags.

url.description: The URL of the LCM repository from which update metadata and images are fetched. For connected-site deployments, this is typically the Nutanix portal URL. For dark-site deployments, this points to a local web server hosting the LCM artifacts.

isAutoInventoryEnabled.description: Controls whether LCM automatically runs a periodic inventory operation. When set to true, LCM will execute inventory at the time specified by autoInventorySchedule. The default value is false.

autoInventorySchedule.description: The scheduled time for automatic inventory execution in 24-hour "%H:%M" format (e.g. "03:00" for 3:00 AM). This field is only relevant when isAutoInventoryEnabled is set to true. The default schedule is 03:00.

version.description: The full build version string of the LCM framework installed on the cluster (e.g. "3.1.45678"). This is a read-only field.

displayVersion.description: A user-friendly display version of the LCM framework (e.g. "3.1"), suitable for presentation in dashboards and reports. This is a read-only field.

connectivityType.description: The connectivity mode under which the LCM framework is operating. Determines how LCM accesses update metadata and images.

isHttpsEnabled.description: Controls whether HTTPS is enforced for communication with the LCM repository URL. The default value is true. Set to false only if the repository does not support HTTPS.

supportedSoftwareEntities.description: Read-only list of software entity names for which One-Click upgrades are supported on this cluster.

deprecatedSoftwareEntities.description: Read-only list of software entity names for which One-Click upgrades are no longer available on this cluster.

isFrameworkBundleUploaded.description: Indicates whether an LCM framework bundle has been uploaded to the cluster. This is a read-only field relevant for dark-site deployments.

hasModuleAutoUpgradeEnabled.description: Controls whether LCM is allowed to automatically upgrade products when updates are available. The default value is false.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.ConnectivityTyp.title: LCM connectivity type

x-enumDescriptions.CONNECTED_SITE: Connected-site mode. The cluster has internet connectivity and LCM downloads modules, metadata, and images directly from the configured portal URL.
x-enumDescriptions.DARKSITE_DIRECT_UPLOAD: Dark-site direct upload mode. The cluster has no external internet connectivity and LCM artifacts (bundles) are uploaded directly to the cluster through the LCM bundle upload API (POST /bundles).
x-enumDescriptions.DARKSITE_WEB_SERVER: Dark-site web server mode. The cluster has no external internet connectivity and connects to a customer-maintained local web server that hosts LCM artifacts.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Entity.title: LCM Entity
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Entity.description: Represents an upgradable software or firmware component discovered by LCM on a cluster. Each entity has a class (e.g. "Core Cluster"), model (e.g. "AOS"), type (SOFTWARE or FIRMWARE), current version, and zero or more available versions for upgrade. The entity also includes location information indicating whether it is scoped to a specific node or the entire cluster.

entityDescription.description: A human-readable description of the LCM entity, providing additional context about the component.

targetVersion.description: The target version that this entity has been selected to upgrade to. This field is set when an upgrade selection or upgrade operation has designated a specific version for this entity. Unset if no upgrade target has been chosen.

lastUpdatedTime.description: The UTC date and time (in RFC-3339 format) when the task was last updated.

deviceId.description: A unique device identifier for the entity, such as a hard drive serial number, NIC serial number, or other hardware-specific identifier.

groupUuid.description: UUID of the entity group that this entity belongs to. Entities in the same group are logically related and may share upgrade dependencies or ordering constraints.

entityDetails.description: Additional key-value metadata specific to the entity type. For example, firmware entities may include NIC vendor, slot number, or PCI address information.

childEntities.description: Component information for payload-based entities. Lists the child entity identifiers that are bundled within this entity's upgrade payload.

availableVersions.description: List of available versions that this entity can be upgraded to. Each entry includes the version string, status, enablement state, dependencies, and release notes. Empty if no updates are available.

subEntities.description: A list of sub-entities associated with this entity. Sub-entities represent components that are logically part of the parent entity (e.g. individual firmware components within a composite firmware entity).

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

hardwareVendor.description: The hardware vendor of the cluster (e.g. "Dell", "HPE", "Lenovo").

hasPreviousInventoryFailed.description: Indicates whether the most recent inventory operation failed for this entity. When true, the entity's version or available-version data may be stale. Re-run inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to refresh.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.AvailableVersio.title: Available version

version.description: The latest LCM framework version available in the configured LCM repository URL. Compare with currentVersion to determine if a framework update is needed.

isEnabled.description: Indicates whether this available version is enabled for upgrade. A version may be disabled if the cluster does not meet the requirements for the update.

availableVersionUuid.description: The UUID of the available version entry.

order.description: The display priority of this available version when multiple versions are present. Lower values indicate higher priority (1 = highest, up to 10000). Useful for ordering version options in a UI.

disablementReason.description: A human-readable explanation of why this available version is disabled. Only present when isEnabled is false.
disablementReason.example: This version is disabled because cluster does not meet the requirements

releaseNotes.description: Release notes for this available version, describing the changes, fixes, and improvements included in the update.

releaseDate.description: The release date of this available version, in ISO 8601 date format.

customMessage.description: A custom message from the vendor about this available version, separate from the release notes. May include advisory notices or special instructions.

childEntities.description: Component information for payload-based entities. Lists the child entity identifiers that are bundled within this entity's upgrade payload.

groupUuid.description: UUID of the entity group that this entity belongs to. Entities in the same group are logically related and may share upgrade dependencies or ordering constraints.

dependencies.description: List of entity dependencies that must be satisfied before upgrading to this version. Each dependency identifies another entity and the version range it must be at.

isImagePresent.description: Indicates whether the upgrade image for this entity is already present on the cluster. When true, the upgrade can proceed without downloading. When false, images must be downloaded or preloaded (POST /$actions/preload-artifacts) before upgrading.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.AvailableVersio.description: The latest LCM framework version available in the configured LCM repository URL. Compare with currentVersion to determine if a framework update is needed.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.LcmHistory.description: Represents a single LCM operation history entry, recording the operation type, start and end times, overall status, the user who initiated the operation, the LCM framework version at execution time, compatibility bundle version, cluster information, and detailed per-component results.

operationType.description: The type of the operation currently in progress.

startTime.description: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when the operation started.

endTime.description: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when the operation completed.

operationStatus.description: The current execution status of an LCM operation.

operationInfo.description: Detailed information about the operation, varying by operation type. For upgrades, this contains per-component upgrade details (UpgradeInfo). For uploads, this contains bundle upload details (UploadInfo). For inventory operations, this contains component discovery details (InventoryInfo).

compatibilityBundleVersion.description: The version of the Nutanix Compatibility (Product Meta) bundle installed on the cluster.

frameworkVersion.description: The LCM framework version that was installed on the cluster when the operation was performed.

clusterName.description: The display name of the cluster on which the operation was performed.

userInfo.description: Information about the user who initiated the operation.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationType.title: LCM operation type
lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationType.description: The type of the operation currently in progress.

x-enumDescriptions.PRECHECKS: Run pre-upgrade validation checks to verify that the cluster and its entities are ready for an upgrade. Prechecks detect conditions that would cause an upgrade to fail, such as insufficient disk space, cluster health issues, incompatible configurations, or pinned VMs that cannot be migrated during host maintenance mode. Submit a PrechecksSpec containing the entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs) that you intend to use for the upgrade. The entityUpdateSpecs should match the output from POST /$actions/compute-recommendations or be manually constructed from GET /entities data. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; inspect the task result to determine whether all prechecks passed. If prechecks fail, address the reported issues before proceeding to POST /$actions/upgrade. Use the skippedPrecheckFlags field to bypass specific prechecks (e.g. the pinned-VM check). Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency.
x-enumDescriptions.INVENTORY: Trigger an inventory operation to discover all upgradable software and firmware entities on a cluster. Inventory scans cluster nodes, identifies installed components and their current versions, and checks the configured LCM repository for available updates. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; poll the task to track progress. Once completed, discovered entities are available via GET /entities and the cluster summary is updated in GET /lcm-summaries. An optional InventorySpec body allows specifying the inventory type and vendor management credentials. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. Only one inventory operation can run on a cluster at a time; check GET /status before invoking. In dark-site mode, inventory discovers available updates only from bundles that have been uploaded to the cluster (POST /bundles); it does not contact the Nutanix portal.
x-enumDescriptions.UPLOAD: Direct upload operation. LCM is processing a bundle uploaded directly to the cluster.
x-enumDescriptions.UPGRADE: Perform an upgrade operation to update one or more LCM entities to their specified target versions. Before invoking an upgrade, ensure you have: (1) run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover entities, (2) computed recommendations (POST /$actions/compute-recommendations) to resolve dependencies and obtain validated entityUpdateSpecs, (3) optionally reviewed notifications (POST /$actions/compute-notifications) to understand the upgrade impact, and (4) run prechecks (POST /$actions/prechecks) to validate cluster readiness. Submit an UpgradeSpec containing the entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs). For ESX or Hyper-V clusters, provide the managementServer credentials. Use autoHandleFlags to allow LCM to automatically power off pinned VMs during maintenance mode and restore them after the upgrade. When operating from Prism Central, supply the X-Cluster-Id header to target a specific Prism Element cluster; if omitted, the operation targets the Prism Central cluster itself. The operation is asynchronous and returns a TaskReference; monitor the task via the Prism tasks API. Use GET /status to check whether an upgrade is already in progress. Only one upgrade can run on a cluster at a time. Requires the NTNX-Request-Id header (a UUID v4 value) for idempotency. In dark-site mode, ensure the required bundles have been uploaded (POST /bundles) before running the upgrade; images are not downloaded from the portal.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: No operation is currently in progress.
x-enumDescriptions.CENTRALIZED_UPLOAD: LCM is centrally processing a bundle uploaded on Prism Central and distributing it to all registered clusters that support the Centralized Uploads feature.
x-enumDescriptions.TARGETED_INVENTORY: Targeted inventory operation. LCM is scanning specific nodes rather than the full cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationStatus.title: Operation status
lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationStatus.description: The current execution status of an LCM operation.

x-enumDescriptions.FAILED: The operation failed. Check the task details for error information.
x-enumDescriptions.QUEUED: The operation is queued and waiting to execute.
x-enumDescriptions.SUSPENDED: The operation has been suspended and is not actively executing.
x-enumDescriptions.CANCELED: The operation was canceled before it completed.
x-enumDescriptions.CANCELING: The operation is in the process of being canceled.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UploadInfo.description: Detailed information about a bundle upload operation, including the bundle name, type, and checksum.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.ComponentDetail.description: Per-component results for the operation, showing which entities were affected and their individual statuses.

deviceId.description: A unique device identifier for the entity, such as a hard drive serial number, NIC serial number, or other hardware-specific identifier.

groupUuid.description: UUID of the entity group that this entity belongs to. Entities in the same group are logically related and may share upgrade dependencies or ordering constraints.

upgradedVersion.description: The version to which the component was upgraded.

hardwareVendor.description: The hardware vendor of the cluster (e.g. "Dell", "HPE", "Lenovo").

inventoryStatus.description: The status of the inventory discovery for this specific component.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.StatusInfo.title: LCM status information
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.StatusInfo.description: Represents the current operational status of the LCM framework on a cluster, including framework version information, any in-progress operation, cancel intent state, URL accessibility, connectivity type, and restricted-mode indicators.

isCancelIntentSet.description: Indicates whether a cancel intent has been set for the current LCM upgrade. When true, LCM will attempt to cancel the ongoing upgrade at the next safe checkpoint.

uploadTaskUuid.description: The task UUID of the in-progress bundle upload operation, if any.

isUrlAccessible.description: Indicates whether the configured LCM repository URL is currently accessible from the cluster. When false, check network connectivity and the URL configuration (GET /config).

isRestrictedMode.description: Indicates whether the LCM framework is operating in restricted mode. In restricted mode, only a subset of operations may be available. See restrictedModeType for the specific restriction reason.

connectivityType.description: The connectivity mode under which the LCM framework is operating. Determines how LCM accesses update metadata and images.

restrictedModeType.description: Indicates the reason why LCM is in restricted mode.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.FrameworkVersio.title: LCM framework version information

currentVersion.description: The version string of the LCM framework currently installed on the cluster.

availableVersion.description: The latest LCM framework version available in the configured LCM repository URL. Compare with currentVersion to determine if a framework update is needed.

isUpdateNeeded.description: Indicates whether the LCM framework needs to be updated to a newer version before performing entity upgrades. When true, update the framework first by running an upgrade operation.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.FrameworkVersio.description: Version information for the LCM framework, including the currently installed version, the latest available version in the repository, and whether an update is needed.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.InProgressOpInf.title: In-progress operation

operationId.description: The root task UUID of the in-progress operation. Use this UUID to monitor the operation via the Prism tasks API.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.InProgressOpInf.description: Information about any LCM operation currently in progress on the cluster, including the operation type and the root task UUID.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.RestrictedModeT.title: Restricted mode type
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.RestrictedModeT.description: Indicates the reason why LCM is in restricted mode.

x-enumDescriptions.NON_UNIFORM_AHV: The cluster has non-uniform AHV versions across nodes. LCM restricts operations until AHV versions are aligned.
x-enumDescriptions.EMERGENCY_UPDATES: The cluster has an emergency update available that must be applied before other upgrades.
x-enumDescriptions.EOL_AOS: The cluster is running an end-of-life AOS or Prism Central version. LCM restricts operations until the platform is updated to a supported version.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.GetNotification.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/notifications/{extId} Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Notification.title: Computed notification result
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Notification.description: The computed upgrade notification result containing notification items grouped by entity and location. Each item includes the entity details, notification type, severity, and descriptive messages about the upgrade impact.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.NotificationIte.title: Notification specification
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.NotificationIte.description: Specification for computing upgrade notifications. Contains the list of entity update specifications (entity UUID and target version pairs) describing the intended upgrade, along with optional credentials for third-party vendor management platforms.

details.description: Detailed notification entries for this item, each containing a severity level and a descriptive message about the upgrade impact.

toVersion.description: The target version that the entity will be upgraded to.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.NotificationType.title: Notification type
lifecycle.v4.3.common.NotificationType.description: The type of the notification, indicating whether it pertains to a specific entity or a location (node/cluster). Supported values are ENTITY and LOCATION.

x-enumDescriptions.LOCATION: Location-scoped notification. The notification describes the upgrade impact for a specific location (node or cluster), such as host reboots or maintenance-mode entry.
x-enumDescriptions.ENTITY: Entity-scoped notification. The notification describes the upgrade impact for a specific entity.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.NotificationDet.title: Notification detail

message.description: A message describing the specific impact, such as the most disruptive action that will occur on the node or cluster during the upgrade.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.NotificationDet.description: A single notification detail entry describing a specific impact of the planned upgrade, with a severity level (INFO, WARNING, or NOTICE) and a message.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.SeverityLevel.title: Notification severity level
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.SeverityLevel.description: The severity classification of an upgrade notification, indicating the level of impact.

x-enumDescriptions.NOTICE: Notice severity. Indicates important information that the user should be aware of but that is not directly disruptive.
x-enumDescriptions.INFO: Informational severity. General information about the upgrade process that does not indicate any disruptive impact.
x-enumDescriptions.WARNING: Warning severity. Indicates a potentially disruptive action such as a host reboot or VM downtime.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.GetRecommendati.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/recommendations/{extId} Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.RecommendationR.title: Recommendation result
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.RecommendationR.description: The computed upgrade recommendation result containing the resolved set of entity update specifications, information about entities that were skipped, modified, or added during dependency resolution, and deployable version details.

entityUpdateSpecs.description: List of entity update specifications (entity UUID and target version pairs) for which to compute recommendations.

skippedEntities.description: List of entities from the input specification that were skipped during recommendation computation, along with the reason for skipping (e.g. entity already at the target version, or incompatible configuration).

modifiableEntities.description: List of entities from the input specification whose target versions were modified during dependency resolution. Each entry includes the adjusted entity information and an explanation message.

addableEntities.description: List of additional entities that must be upgraded alongside the requested entities to satisfy dependency requirements. These entities were not in the original input but are required for a valid upgrade plan.

deployableVersions.description: List of deployable entity versions and their dependencies, indicating which images need to be staged on the cluster for the recommended upgrades.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpdatedTargetEn.title: Target entity result

targetEntity.description: Identifies a specific entity for recommendation computation using its class, model, and desired target version. Optionally includes location information and device identifier for disambiguation when multiple instances of the same entity exist.

message.description: A message explaining the reason for skipping, modifying, or adding the entity during recommendation computation.
message.example: Entity has been updated based on compatibility

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpdatedTargetEn.description: Result entry for a target entity in the recommendation computation, including a message explaining why the entity was skipped, modified, or added.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.DeployableVersi.title: Deployable version
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.DeployableVersi.description: Represents an entity version that can be deployed (pre-staged) on the cluster, along with its update dependencies.

targetVersion.description: The target version for the entity upgrade.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpdatedTargetEn.title: Updated target entity
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpdatedTargetEn.description: An entity whose target version or inclusion was adjusted during recommendation computation.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.ListLcmSummarie.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/lcm-summaries Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.LcmSummary.title: LCM cluster summary
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.LcmSummary.description: A high-level summary of the LCM state on a cluster, including framework version, hardware vendor, connectivity type, capabilities, and upgrade availability indicators.

currentVersion.description: The version string of the LCM framework currently installed on the cluster.

availableVersion.description: The latest LCM framework version available in the configured LCM repository URL. Compare with currentVersion to determine if a framework update is needed.

hardwareVendor.description: The hardware vendor of the cluster (e.g. "Dell", "HPE", "Lenovo").

capabilities.description: List of capabilities supported by LCM on this cluster. Capabilities indicate which advanced features are available, such as multi-cluster lifecycle (MCL) inventory, MCL upgrades, unified uploads, and targeted inventory.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

isUrlAccessible.description: Indicates whether the configured LCM repository URL is currently accessible from the cluster. When false, check network connectivity and the URL configuration (GET /config).

compatibilityBundleVersion.description: The version of the Nutanix Compatibility (Product Meta) bundle installed on the cluster.

connectivityType.description: The connectivity mode under which the LCM framework is operating. Determines how LCM accesses update metadata and images.

clusterType.description: Indicates whether the cluster is a Prism Central or a Prism Element cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.HostInventoryTi.title: Host inventory time

time.description: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when inventory was last performed on this host.

nodeExtId.description: The UUID of the host (node) for which this inventory time is recorded.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.HostInventoryTi.description: The timestamp of the last inventory operation for a specific host (node) in the cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Capability.title: Cluster capability
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.Capability.description: A capability flag indicating a specific feature supported by LCM on this cluster.

x-enumDescriptions.MCL_UPGRADE: Multi-cluster lifecycle (MCL) upgrade capability. When present, the cluster supports centralized upgrade operations initiated from Prism Central.
x-enumDescriptions.MCL_INVENTORY: Multi-cluster lifecycle (MCL) inventory capability. When present, the cluster supports centralized inventory operations initiated from Prism Central.
x-enumDescriptions.MCL_UNIFIED_UPLOADS: Multi-cluster lifecycle (MCL) unified uploads capability. When present, the cluster supports centralized bundle uploads from Prism Central.
x-enumDescriptions.TARGETED_INVENTORY: Targeted inventory capability. When present, the cluster supports running inventory on specific nodes rather than the full cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.InProgressOpDetail.title: In-progress operation details

taskExtId.description: The task UUID of the in-progress LCM operation. Use this UUID to monitor progress via the Prism tasks API.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.InProgressOpDetail.description: Details of an LCM operation currently in progress on a cluster, including the operation type and the task identifier.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationCredentia.title: Operation credential

credentialExtId.description: The UUID of the credential stored in the credential store.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.OperationCredentia.description: Describes a credential configured for a cluster, including its reference in the credential store, the vendor management platform it authenticates with, and which operation types it supports.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.ClusterType.title: Cluster type
lifecycle.v4.3.common.ClusterType.description: Indicates whether the cluster is a Prism Central or a Prism Element cluster.

lifecycle.v4.3.common.VendorManagementNa.title: Vendor management name
lifecycle.v4.3.common.VendorManagementNa.description: The name of the third-party vendor management software that manages the server fleet. Identifies which credential type is required.

x-enumDescriptions.ISM: Cisco Intersight. A third-party cloud-based server management platform for Cisco hardware.
x-enumDescriptions.UCS: Cisco UCS Manager. A third-party server management platform for Cisco UCS hardware.
x-enumDescriptions.VCENTER: VMware vCenter Server. A management platform for ESXi hypervisor hosts.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.GetLcmSummaryBy.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/lcm-summaries/{extId} Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.GetUpgradeSelec.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/upgrade-selections/{extId} Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.DeleteUpgradeSe.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/upgrade-selections/{extId} Delete operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpgradeSelectio.title: Upgrade selection
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpgradeSelectio.description: Represents a saved set of entity upgrade selections for a cluster. Used in dark-site workflows to capture the intended upgrades, generate download helpers for obtaining required bundles, and track readiness status.

selectedUpgrades.description: The list of selected entity upgrades (entity UUID and target version pairs) that the user intends to perform.

clusterExtId.description: The cluster UUID on which the resource is present or the operation is being performed.

status.description: The current status of the upgrade selection, indicating whether all required bundles have been uploaded.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpgradeSelectio.title: Upgrade selection status
lifecycle.v4.3.resources.UpgradeSelectio.description: The current status of the upgrade selection, indicating whether all required bundles have been uploaded.

x-enumDescriptions.UPGRADE_READY: All required images have been uploaded and the cluster is ready for upgrade. Proceed with POST /$actions/prechecks and POST /$actions/upgrade using the saved entityUpdateSpecs.
x-enumDescriptions.STALE_SELECTION: The saved selection is stale, meaning the cluster state has changed since the selection was created (e.g. a new inventory was run or entities changed). Create a new selection to ensure accuracy.
x-enumDescriptions.PENDING_UPLOAD: The selection is awaiting upload of all required images. Use POST /bundles to upload the necessary dark-site bundles.

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.ListUpgradeSele.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/upgrade-selections Get operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.CreateUpgradeSe.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/upgrade-selections Post operation

lifecycle.v4.3.resources.ExportUpgradeSe.description: REST response for all response codes in API path /lifecycle/v4.3/resources/upgrade-selections/{extId}/$actions/export Post operation

allOf.title: VCenter Credential.
allOf.description: A credential used for authentication with VCenter server.

secretKey.description: Secret key of the Intersight connection.

security.v4.1.config.KeyBasedAuth.description: Secret fields of a Key based Authencation credential.

username.description: Username required for the basic auth scheme. As per [RFC 2617](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2617) usernames might be case sensitive.

password.description: Password required for the basic auth scheme.

common.v1.0.config.BasicAuth.description: An authentication scheme that requires the client to present a username and password. The server will service the request only if it can validate the user-ID and password for the protection space of the Request-URI.

nonMigratableVmReason.description: Reason for a VM to be non-migratable.
